summary: Round 2, tests. All THREE round-1 majors verified DEAD by measurement: putIfAbsent -> unconditional put now killed by whenTwoNodesBothSeeAnAbsentLeaseExactlyOneWinsTheConditionalWrite (which also reaches adopt's losing branch for the first time); deleting heldVersion = won.get() killed by aHolderCanRenewRepeatedlyBecauseItRecordsEachNewVersion; takeover adopting the version it CASed FROM killed by aNodeThatTookOverCanThenRenew. Of the four claimed-fixed minors, three verified dead (blank podId guard, renew's fenced belief-clearing, the whole renewInterval positivity guard) and TWO did not: adopt's OWN belief-clearing survives deletion 26/26, and the ttl positivity guard survives deletion ENTIRELY 26/26. StatBlind is sound -- it models a real stat/CAS interleaving and the win/lose arbitration still comes from the real MemoryBinStore, not the decorator. Suite 480/0 confirmed by running it; 26 red records present, one per test. Six minors below, each with a measured surviving mutation. No major raised: review.md rule 12's remedy for a round-2 blocker is to SPLIT the commit, and a one-class change with one test file is not too big -- every finding here is a small test addition, not a decomposition.

findings.title: adopt's OWN belief-clearing is unconstrained -- and the backlog row claims it was measured dead
findings.mutation: Delete `held = null; heldVersion = null;` from adopt's `won.isEmpty()` branch (LeaseManager.java:207-208), leaving `return Optional.empty();`. MEASURED: 26 tests, 0 failures, gradle exit 0. SURVIVES.
findings.failure_scenario: This is the exact line the round-1 production minor added, and backlog.md:220 says of it 'a LOST takeover now drops the stale belief exactly as `renew` does, so `held()` cannot report a term this instance does not hold ... All four mutations verified dead.' It is not dead. The two tests named as covering it -- heldReportsWhatThisInstanceActuallyHolds (LeaseManagerTest.java:396) and aFencedHolderStopsBelievingItHoldsTheLease (LeaseManagerTest.java:408) -- both reach the clearing in `renew`, never in `adopt`; I confirmed this by deleting renew's clearing separately, which IS killed by :408. No test reaches adopt's losing branch with a non-null prior belief: in whenTwoNodesBothSeeAnAbsentLeaseExactlyOneWinsTheConditionalWrite the loser `b` has held == null already. Production interleaving that distinguishes it: A holds a lease that has expired; A calls tryAcquire to re-take it; between A's stat and A's putIfMatch, B takes over; A's CAS loses; without the clearing A.held() keeps returning A's old term. A caller gating 'may I sequence?' on held().isPresent() -- which is what a leader loop will do at M4.6/M4.7 -- then sequences while B holds the term. That is two nodes sequencing at once, the invariant this task exists to protect. Blast radius TODAY is zero because no caller exists yet, which is why this is a minor rather than a major. Cheap to close: the StatBlind decorator already in the file reaches it in two lines -- acquire once (wins putIfAbsent, held set), acquire again (stat still blind, putIfAbsent now loses), assert held() is empty. Alternatively argue it in baselines/mutants.txt per testing.md rule 9. Either way the sentence in backlog.md:220 must stop saying it was verified.
findings.remedy: Add a test reaching adopt's losing branch with a prior belief (StatBlind, acquire twice), or argue the mutant; and correct 'All four mutations verified dead' in backlog.md:220.

findings.title: Both ttl-positivity tests are EQUIVALENT-MUTANT tests: the whole ttl guard is deletable, 26/26 green
findings.mutation: (a) `ttl.isZero() || ttl.isNegative()` -> `ttl.isZero()`: 26/26 green, SURVIVES. (b) Delete the entire `if (ttl.isZero() || ttl.isNegative()) { throw ... }` block: 26/26 green, SURVIVES. Both measured.
findings.failure_scenario: aNonPositiveTtlIsRefused (:258) and the ttl leg of aNegativeTtlOrRenewIntervalIsRefused (:422) assert only `hasMessageContaining("ttl")`. With the ttl guard gone, a ttl of ZERO or -1s falls through to the renewInterval-vs-ttl guard, whose message is 'renewInterval must be shorter than ttl: PT1S >= PT0S' -- which also contains the substring 'ttl'. The assertion passes for the wrong reason and does not pin WHICH guard fired. This is verbatim the class M4.3 round 2 spent a round closing ('the three shape-guard tests were EQUIVALENT MUTANTS, green under every individual guard deletion ... now assert the message, pinning which guard fired'), and the comment the author added at LeaseManagerTest.java:424 asserts the opposite: 'The ZERO case alone left ttl.isNegative() deletable' -- implying the new test kills it. It does not. Note the red records do not catch this: both tests have a red record, earned against a skeleton with no constructor validation at all, which proves they fail when NOTHING throws, not that they discriminate this guard. Consequence in production is bounded -- the (ttl<=0, renewInterval>0) pair is still refused by the other guard -- so what is lost is the operator-facing diagnosis of a misconfigured negative TTL, not safety. One-string fix: assert `hasMessageContaining("ttl must be positive")`, which I verified would kill both mutations (the fallback message does not contain that phrase).
findings.remedy: Tighten the two ttl assertions to the guard's own message phrase, or delete the comment at :424 that claims a property the test does not have.

findings.title: The endpoint is pinned on the cold-start path only; the TAKEOVER path can still discard it
findings.mutation: `current.takenOverBy(podId, endpoint, ...)` -> `current.takenOverBy(podId, "", ...)` at LeaseManager.java:143. MEASURED: 26 tests, 0 failures. SURVIVES. (The same substitution at line 133, the first-acquisition path, IS killed by theEndpointIsWrittenIntoTheLeaseRatherThanDiscarded.)
findings.failure_scenario: theEndpointIsWrittenIntoTheLeaseRatherThanDiscarded acquires against an empty store, so it exercises putIfAbsent only. Every term after the very first one in a cluster's life is reached by takeover -- that is the failover path, the half that matters -- and on that path the endpoint can be dropped with the suite green. The consequence lands at M5: commit forwarding must REACH the holder, and the row's stated reason for carrying holderEndpoint from the first lease is exactly so M5 is not a format change. A failover leader that publishes an empty endpoint is unreachable, and no test in this milestone would say so. Nil impact today because holderEndpoint is documented as empty throughout M4. Fix is one line: give the test a second manager that takes over after clock.advance(TTL) with a distinct endpoint, and assert it.
findings.remedy: Extend :449 to cover the takeover path with a second, distinct endpoint.

findings.title: acquiringCostsOneReadAndOneWriteAndRenewingCostsOneWrite asserts only the renew half its name claims
findings.mutation: Insert two extra `store.stat(key);` calls before line 130 of LeaseManager.java so tryAcquire issues THREE stats. MEASURED: 26 tests, 0 failures. SURVIVES.
findings.failure_scenario: The test captures `afterAcquire = store.counts().total()` and asserts only the DELTA across renew, so the acquisition cost it names is unconstrained -- the acquire could cost three reads, or thirty, with the suite green. This is a cost.md lens: a standby node polls tryAcquire once per renew interval forever, so an extra stat per tryAcquire is a per-node, per-interval request multiplier on an idle cluster (testing.md rule 22: 'zero requests from an idle cluster ... the one failure invisible to every functional test'). It does not scale with records or indices, so it is not a non-negotiable-6 breach, but the test literally names the number it does not check. theFirstAcquisitionUsesPutIfAbsent... (:82) constrains the acquire WRITE count at 1; nothing constrains the acquire READ count. Fix: assert `afterAcquire` equals 2 (one stat, one put).
findings.remedy: Assert the acquire total as well as the renew delta, or rename the test to what it checks.

findings.title: renewingWithoutEverHavingAcquiredIsRefused pins the return value but not the side effect -- a destructive write survives
findings.mutation: In renew's `if (held == null)` branch, add `store.put(key, Body.ofBytes(new Lease(0, podId, endpoint, clock.millis()).encode()));` before `return Optional.empty();`. MEASURED: 26 tests, 0 failures. SURVIVES.
findings.failure_scenario: Under that mutant a NON-HOLDER calling renew() unconditionally overwrites ctl/lease/0.json with an expired epoch-0 lease: it destroys the fencing counter (the very thing releaseKeepsTheEpochSoTheNextHolderStillAdvancesIt exists to protect), and it instantly un-leads the real holder, whose next renew then CASes against a version this write superseded. The sibling test releasingWhenNotHeldIsAHarmlessNoOpRatherThanAnError (:198) does assert `counts().total()` is zero; this one asserts only Optional emptiness. In fairness the PLAUSIBLE mutation -- deleting the `held == null` guard outright -- is killed (NPE on held.renewedUntil), so the guard itself is pinned; what is unpinned is that the branch is a pure no-op. One line closes it: wrap in CountingBinStore and assert total() is zero, exactly as :198 does.
findings.remedy: Use CountingBinStore and assert zero requests, matching the release sibling.

findings.title: The `synchronized` the row calls load-bearing has no test
findings.mutation: Replace all four `public synchronized` with `public`. MEASURED: 26 tests, 0 failures. SURVIVES.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md:220 states 'and `synchronized` for the same reason (the read-decide-CAS cycle must not interleave with itself)' as a property of the change, and testing.md rule 13 asks that every acceptance criterion have a test that would fail without it. Two threads calling tryAcquire on ONE manager instance with the modifier removed can interleave stat/decide/CAS and both reach adopt, and given the read-modify-write on `held`/`heldVersion` the loser can overwrite the winner's belief. I am NOT asking for a thread test: a deterministic one at T1 is expensive and a non-deterministic one is worse than none, which is why this is a minor. The honest resolutions are an argued entry in baselines/mutants.txt per testing.md rule 9, or M4.12's deterministic simulation adopting it. Recording it so it is not mistaken for covered.
findings.remedy: Argue the mutant in baselines/mutants.txt, or hand it to M4.12's simulation.

findings.title: aFencedHolderCannotRenewAndLearnsItFromTheEmptyResult is now strictly subsumed by aFencedHolderStopsBelievingItHoldsTheLease
findings.mutation: No mutation is killed by :144 that is not also killed by :408 -- identical setup (A acquires, clock advances TTL, B takes over), and :408 asserts everything :144 asserts (renew() is empty) plus one more (held() is empty). Confirmed by inspection and by the fact that every mutation I ran which killed :144 also killed :408.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a defect -- it is the only redundancy I found in the 26, and it is the answer to the packet's question 'any now redundant after the additions'. The cost of keeping it is one more test to maintain and one more name that reads as independent coverage when it is not; the benefit is that its javadoc carries the gray-failure rationale, which :408's does not. I would keep it and NOT act on this, per rule 11. Recording it only so the count of 26 is not read as 26 independent constraints.
findings.remedy: None recommended. Keep both, or fold :144's rationale comment into :408.

verified_from_previous_round: MAJOR 1 putIfAbsent -> Optional.of(store.put(...)): KILLED by whenTwoNodesBothSeeAnAbsentLeaseExactlyOneWinsTheConditionalWrite. Separately, adopt's losing branch replaced by `throw new AssertionError`: KILLED by the same test, so the branch is now genuinely reached.
MAJOR 2 delete `heldVersion = won.get()` in renew: KILLED by aHolderCanRenewRepeatedlyBecauseItRecordsEachNewVersion.
MAJOR 3 takeover adopts stat.get().version() instead of the won version: KILLED by aNodeThatTookOverCanThenRenew.
minor: blank podId guard -> `if (false)`: KILLED by aBlankPodIdIsRefusedAtConstructionRatherThanAtTheFirstAcquire.

minor: renew's fenced branch no longer clears held/heldVersion: KILLED by aFencedHolderStopsBelievingItHoldsTheLease. (The previously-open 'renew-fenced clearing has no test of its own' minor is now CLOSED.)
minor: whole renewInterval positivity guard deleted: KILLED by aNegativeTtlOrRenewIntervalIsRefused.
minor: endpoint discarded on the FIRST-acquisition path: KILLED by theEndpointIsWrittenIntoTheLeaseRatherThanDiscarded.
NOT killed, see findings: adopt's own belief-clearing; the entire ttl positivity guard; the endpoint on the TAKEOVER path.

StatBlind soundness: SOUND. It models a real interleaving -- stat and the conditional write are two round trips, and on S3 a HEAD can also be served stale -- so 'stat says absent, putIfAbsent finds it present' is a state production can reach and must lose gracefully in. Crucially the win/lose arbitration comes from the real MemoryBinStore's putIfAbsent, not from the decorator, so the test cannot pass for a reason production could not produce. It is a fake decorating a fake, satisfying testing.md rule 18.

Tier and testing.md compliance: T1 throughout, MemoryBinStore, Clock injected and advanced never slept on, no Thread.sleep, no ports, no system temp. Non-negotiable 7 satisfied -- the manager takes Clock and BinStore as seams.

Suite: ran `./gradlew test`, 480 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped -- the row's 480 is honest. check-tdd: 26 red records under binjava.sequencer.LeaseManagerTest, one per test, matching the 26 in the file. Caveat noted in the ttl finding: a red record proves a test failed against the skeleton, not that it discriminates a specific guard.

Backlog row honesty: honest on the three majors, on 480, and on the ambiguous-renew deferral. FALSE on 'All four mutations verified dead' -- see the first finding. The 'endpoint is now pinned as written into the lease' claim is defensible only if the mutation was applied to both call sites; it is half-width in practice.

Ambiguous renew (PUT lands, response lost, holder self-fences for up to a TTL): AGREED as recorded-not-fixed. It is the same class as M4.1's ambiguous IOException that M4.10 owns, recovery is bounded by the TTL failover the spec already accepts, and the lease is liveness not safety (ADR-0002), so the cost is an outage window and never a lost write. One note for whoever takes M4.10: the fake needed to test it -- a store that LANDS the write and then throws -- does not exist in testFixtures yet, so M4.10 must ship it alongside.

Two-nodes-at-once / sequencing-after-loss sweep: the conditional-write nature of every transition is now pinned (acquisition by the StatBlind test, renew by aFencedHolderCannotRenew..., release by aFencedHolderCannotReleaseSomeoneElsesLease, takeover by aNodeThatTookOverCanThenRenew), and the expiry boundary is pinned on both sides (TTL-1ms not stolen, TTL exactly stolen). The one remaining hole in that class is adopt's stale belief, filed as the first finding.
